newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish export guarantee firm to double premiums.
newsitem.headline: Polish export guarantee firm to double premiums.

text.p: Poland's state-controlled Credit Exports Insurance Corporation (KUKE), which collected 13 million zloty in premiums in 1996, expects to double the sum this year, the president of the firm said on Tuesday.
"In 1996 we collected 13 million zlotys in premium...this year we want to double the collected premium," Krzysztof Jasinski told a news conference.
Jasinski said the company had a net profit of 7.3 million zlotys in 1996 and in the first quarter of 1997 it had a net profit of 1.1 million zlotys. @
KUKE which has the mission of supporting Poland's exports, said chemical, metals traders and construction firms dominated among its clients.
KUKE's main shareholders are the finance ministry with 80.8 percent of shares and the National Bank of Poland, the central bank, which has 14.5 percent.
